answer: In the proportional-odds ordinal regression of COVID-19 severity (per-patient max AESEV, 1-4) on BCG status and prior medical history, controlling for patient interaction frequency (patients_seen), the BCG x prior-medical-history interaction was NOT statistically significant: OR = 1.07 (95% CI 0.62-1.86), coefficient = +0.071, p = 0.799 (N = 791). There is no evidence that the effect of BCG vaccination on severity differs between patients with and without prior medical history. Main effects: BCG OR = 1.50 (95% CI 1.01-2.23, p = 0.045, i.e. BCG associated with ~50% higher odds of a more severe category); prior medical history OR = 1.36 (95% CI 0.90-2.05, p = 0.139); patients_seen OR = 0.986 (95% CI 0.74-1.32, p = 0.924). MLE converged; the proportional-odds assumption was rejected by the Brant test (chi2 = 197.9, df = 10, p < 0.0001), so the interaction OR should be read as an approximation (a partial-proportional-odds model would relax this).
